instrument.state: A sample contains multiple components whose interactions with two phases differ enough that those components need not move together.
instrument.operation: Carry the sample through a system containing a moving phase and a stationary phase so that components repeatedly partition between them.
instrument.signal: Components migrate at different rates and emerge at different positions or times, producing separated bands or detector peaks.
instrument.inference: The separation pattern supports the presence of distinguishable components with different partition behavior and permits their relative retention to be characterized.
instrument.limit: Components with similar partition behavior may co-elute, operating conditions can shift retention, detector response may be nonspecific, and retention behavior alone generally does not establish chemical identity without appropriate standards or orthogonal evidence.

target.question: Determine which components can be distinguished and what evidence supports that decomposition.
evidence: A team studies a proposal composed of interwoven idea fragments. The evidence consists of proposal texts and free-form discussion, without an established circulation, retention, and release workflow.

mapping.state: Proposal as a mixture; fragments as components; a moving phase (some vehicle that carries the whole proposal forward, e.g., successive rounds or audiences) and a stationary phase (some medium that differentially retains fragments); a detector that registers which fragments have emerged. Each fragment has a partition affinity toward the stationary versus moving phase; fragments with different affinity separate, those with similar affinity co-elute; relative retention orders fragments. Repeated partitioning as the proposal is carried through the medium; fragments migrate at different rates; separation accumulates with passes.
mapping.operation: Design and run a circulation-retention-release workflow: pass the proposal through a sequence of contexts or holders, record which fragments are retained and which move on at each stage, adjust conditions and repeat.
mapping.signal: Emergence order or position of fragments (retention profile), band width or sharpness, co-emergence of fragments, shifts in profile under changed conditions.
mapping.inference: Fragments that emerge separately are distinguishable components; their relative retention characterizes them; co-emerging fragments are not shown to be distinct by this run.
mapping.limit: Co-elution of genuinely distinct fragments; retention shifts with framing, order, or audience; the detector registers presence without meaning; retention pattern alone does not say what a fragment is or whether it is one idea or several.
